question.problem:
The parabola $y={x}^{2}$ and the line $y=9x-14$ intersect at the points $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})$ and $({x}_{2},{y}_{2}),$ where ${x}_{1}<{x}_{2}.$ Find the values of ${y}_{1}$ and ${y}_{2}.$

${y}_{1}=$
{{field-1}}$,\,{y}_{2}=$
{{field-2}}
question.worked_solution:
We need to solve the following system consisting of the equations of the curves:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}y={x}^{2} \\ y=9x-14\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the equations equal to one another and solving, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2} & =9x-14 \\ {x}^{2}-9x+14 & =0 \\ (x-2)(x-7) & =0 \\ x & =2,7.\end{aligned}
$$

Since ${x}_{1}<{x}_{2},$ the $x$-coordinates of the intersection points are ${x}_{1}=2$ and ${x}_{2}=7.$

To find the $y$-coordinates of the intersection points, we plug these values into either curve. Let's choose the parabola since it's simpler.

- Substituting ${x}_{1}=2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & ={x}_{1}^{2} \\  & =(2)^{2} \\  & =4,\end{aligned}
$$

so one point of intersection is $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(2,4).$

- Substituting ${x}_{2}=7,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{2} & ={x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =(7)^{2} \\  & =49,\end{aligned}
$$

so the other point of intersection is $({x}_{2},{y}_{2})=(7,49).$
